items.description: The capital and largest city of Argentina, known for its European-style architecture and vibrant tango scene.
A planned city known for its unique grid pattern, diagonal avenues, and iconic neo-Gothic cathedral.
Argentina's premier seaside resort city, famous for its extensive sandy beaches and busy harbor.
A significant port city and industrial center located in southern Buenos Aires Province.
A scenic city nestled in the Tandilia mountain range, famous for its hilly landscapes and salami production.
A historic industrial city located within the Greater Buenos Aires metropolitan area.
A densely populated city known for its residential character and significant urban development in Greater Buenos Aires.
An affluent northern suburb of Buenos Aires, known for its colonial heritage and riverside mansions.
A strategic city on the Paraná River, known for its steel industry and significant religious shrine.
A bustling industrial and residential city, serving as a key transit point in the southern suburbs.
